methods.label: Group the base-three digits in pairs
methods.explanation:
Because \(9=3^2\), moving one place in base nine has the same effect as moving two places in base three. We can therefore convert by grouping base-three digits in pairs from the right:
\[
12\mid11\mid22\mid11\mid12\mid22\mid11\mid11\mid22\mid22.
\]
Each pair has a value from \(0\) through \(8\), so it becomes one valid base-nine digit. There are \(20\) base-three digits, and the leading pair is \(12\). Its value is
\[
1\cdot3+2=5.
\]
Thus the first base-nine digit is \(5\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
